## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The `--json` default destination must be fixed before merge: it works only when `--json` is the last argument, so placing it before `--junit` fails or writes to a file named after the flag.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `--json` option to `parse_args` in `app/cli.py`, with a default destination of `results.json` or an explicit path, and a `write_reports` function that writes each report to its parsed destination. It also adds `tests/test_cli.py` covering the JSON default, an explicit JSON path, and the `--junit` path requirement.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — Stop --json from consuming a following flag as its path — `parse_args(["--json", "--junit", "out.xml"])` stores `"--junit"` as the JSON destination and then raises `ValueError("unknown option: out.xml")`. Line 15 checks only `i + 1 < len(args)`, unlike the `startswith("--")` check at line 7. `["--json", "--junit"]` returns `{"json": "--junit"}`, so `write_reports` writes a file named `--junit`. — Users who pass `--json` before `--junit` get a misleading error or a misnamed output file and no JUnit destination. — Fix: Take the next argument as the path only when `i + 1 < len(args) and not args[i + 1].startswith("--")`, and extend `test_json_default_and_explicit_path` with the `--json`-before-`--junit` order.
